title: BatteryLedger sensor profile
description: How to find the sensors BatteryLedger needs among the entities created by one Home Assistant integration.

platform.description: Entity registry platform of the sensors (the integration domain, or 'mqtt' for MQTT discovery).

brands.description: Battery brands (as used in specs) this profile applies to. An integration that works with several brands (e.g. Energy Manager) lists each of them.

install_date.description: A date helper holding the first battery group's install / warranty start date; pre-fills setup.

install_cost.description: A number helper holding what the first battery group cost; pre-fills setup.

install_date_2.description: Install / warranty start date of batteries added later (the second battery group).

install_cost_2.description: What the batteries added later (the second battery group) cost.

brand.description: An entity naming the system's brand (e.g. an inverter brand selector). Its rule's `values` maps each state to the battery brands it can mean.

module_count.description: Number of battery modules (per tower when tower_count is given). Used to suggest the battery model and unit count.

tower_count.description: Number of battery towers / stacks, each with module_count modules.

inverter_model.description: Inverter model text (e.g. 'SigenStor EC 30.0 TP AU'), per inverter. Its words are matched against spec model lines (series).

inverter_pack_count.description: Number of battery modules on each inverter.

inverter_rated_capacity.description: Rated battery capacity on each inverter (kWh or Wh). With the pack count it gives the capacity per module.

pack_serial.description: One rule per battery pack position on an inverter; positions with a serial number are counted as installed modules. The serial itself is never stored.

unavailable.description: Sensors this integration has a rule for but can't provide for some battery brands, because those batteries don't report them through it (e.g. Huawei Solar: SoH only from a SmartLogger, never from a LUNA2000). Role -> brands. Roles the profile has no rule for are unavailable for every brand anyway.

template.description: unique_id template. Placeholders for parts that differ between installs: {entry} {device} {prefix} {plant} {inverter} {station} {serial} {mac}. An integration with fixed unique IDs needs none. Everything else is literal.

system_rules.description: Matching rules in order of preference.

default_entity_ids.description: Entity IDs the integration creates for this sensor with its default naming, newest first, shown on the Store site. Not used for matching (that's unique_id). Use <serial> etc. for install-specific parts.

platform.description: Entity registry platform for this rule, when it differs from integration.platform (e.g. input_datetime for a helper).

values.description: For the brand role: entity state -> battery brands (as used in specs) it can mean. States not listed fall back to the profile's brands.

default_entity_ids.description: Entity IDs the integration creates for this sensor with its default naming, newest first, shown on the Store site. Not used for matching (that's unique_id). Use <serial> etc. for install-specific parts.

inverter_rules.description: Per-inverter rules: every match is kept, one set per inverter (the placeholders other than entry/prefix/plant/mac tell inverters apart).

default_entity_ids.description: Entity IDs the integration creates for this sensor with its default naming, newest first, shown on the Store site. Not used for matching (that's unique_id). Use <serial> etc. for install-specific parts.

platform.description: Entity registry platform for this rule, when it differs from integration.platform (e.g. input_datetime for a helper).

tower.description: For pack_serial: which battery tower (stack) on the inverter this pack position is in, counted from 1. Detect then offers one battery group per tower. Leave out when the integration doesn't tell towers apart.
